summary: Custom memory copy (memmove-like): copies a3 bytes from source a2 to destination a1 and returns the destination address a1. When the destination overlaps the source range (a1 > a2 && a1 < a2 + a3) the function copies backward from the end to avoid clobbering source data; otherwise it copies forward. The forward path performs DWORD-aligned bulk copies (a qmemcpy for large sizes plus an unrolled 0..7 DWORD switch) and finishes with byte-granular remainder copies; an unaligned destination is first brought to alignment through jump-table-dispatched loops (jpt_58CC5C / jpt_58CC35). All loc_/byte_ globals are jump-table data and case targets of the Duff's-device-style dispatch.

operations.description: Detect source/destination overlap: when a1 > (unsigned)a2 and a1 < (unsigned)(a2 + a3) the destination lies inside the source range and the backward-copy path is taken.
Backward path setup: seed end-of-range pointers v7 = (int)&a2[a3 - 4] and v8 = a3 + a1 - 4.
Backward bulk copy: while v9 = a3 >> 2 is non-zero, copy DWORDs from v7 to v8 and step both pointers back by 4, entering the loop only when a3 >> 2 >= 8.

Backward tail copy: dispatch through the jpt_58CDE4 / jpt_58CDC2 jump tables (entry data byte_58CDE8 / byte_58CDF8, case targets loc_58CE94..loc_58CED7 and loc_58CEF0..loc_58CF1C) and copy the remaining 0..3 bytes at v8+3, v8+2, v8+1 from the matching source tail bytes.

Forward path destination-alignment check: when (a1 & 3) != 0 dispatch through the jpt_58CC5C table (entry byte_58CC60, small-size entry loc_58CD58 / jpt_58CC35) to align the destination before bulk copying.
Unaligned-destination alignment loop: copy leading bytes until the destination is DWORD-aligned, loop body at loc_58CC70.

Forward bulk copy: for 4 * v5 >= 8 bytes use qmemcpy(a1, a2, 4 * v5); otherwise dispatch through the unrolled 0..7 DWORD switch (entry loc_58CC9C, completion loc_58CCC0, case targets loc_58CCFC..loc_58CD3F).
Forward tail copy: switch on a3 & 3 and copy the 0..3 remainder bytes from v3 to v4 (bytes v4[0], v4[1], v4[2] at destination offsets 0x0, 0x1, 0x2).
Return the destination address a1 in all copy paths.
